 ‘It isn’t like he shuns Duke’: Inside Miami QB Darian Mensah’s transfer decisions on road to Coral Gables
 Morgan Moriarty
 • 
 SN
 Add Sporting News on Google 
 div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> 
 The Miami Hurricanes suffered their first loss of the season last week on the road to Notre Dame. Despite missing his favorite target in Malachi Toney, Canes starting quarterback Darian Mensah played well.
 He will look to get his team back on track as it takes on Duke in Week 11, and Mensah will be playing against a team he knows well. Mensah played as recently as last season for the Blue Devils before he transferred to Miami ahead of the 2026 season.
 Mensah actually has plenty of experience playing against a former team, as he played against his previous team, Tulane, when he was at Duke last season.
 MORE:   How Malachi Toney, Julian Sayin injuries shake up wide open Heisman race 
 Why did Darian Mensah leave Duke?
 Mensah played the 2024 season at Tulane before transferring to Duke ahead of the 2025 season. He had a great season with the Blue Devils, leading them to a surprise ACC title game, which his team won 27-20 in overtime over Virginia, giving Duke its first outright ACC title since 1962.
 Mensah played at Duke through the Blue Devils' Sun Bowl against Arizona State, which Duke won 42-39. He threw for 327 yards with four touchdowns and an interception in the win.
 But even before Duke's bowl game, Mensah had confirmed he would return to the Blue Devils in 2026. He even signed a new deal with the school, reportedly around $8 million across two seasons. 
 However, at at the end of January, Mensah entered the transfer portal instead. The decision surprised even his Blue Devil teammate, Duke running back Nate Sheppard, was taken aback. 
 "I remember Darian called me and was like, 'I just got this crazy offer,'" Sheppard said in a recent interview with CBS Sports . "And I was like, well, you know, you got to do what's best for you. If you think that's best, then go ahead. But obviously, it was a little frustrating. We were supposed to come back, kind of repeat things."
 Mensah also ended up bringing Duke leading receiver Cooper Brkate with him to Coral Gables. Duke head coach Manny Diaz said "everyone was surprised" of the decision of Mensah entering the portal. 
 "It was turbulent," Diaz added via ESPN . "All of them got called [by other teams] and the whole thing could've gone kaput. The leadership of our guys to hold tight and stay was massive. I think they were shaken, but they believe now."
 His exit from Duke was a bit messy. After Mensah announced he had committed to Miami on social media , the school initially sued Mensah in Durham County Superior Court. The school wanted to both enforce the multi-year NIL agreement he signed with the school, and prevent him from leaving. 
 But the school entered his name into the portal, and the Duke and the quarterback later settled on the lawsuit , allowing Mensah to freely go to Miami. 
 Mensah contended "business is business" when asked about his decision to go to Miami at ACC Media Days in July. His mother, Naomi Brebes-Mensah, echoed that sentiment. 
 "People were dragging Darian for thinking it was all about money. It wasn't. There was money either way, his mother said via Yahoo Sports . "We looked at the big picture of where Darian wants to go. That ultimately was the choice. What was going to get him to his end goal? He could go and win the ACC again but could he get to a natty and win the Heisman?"
 It was reported that Mensah is making $6.5 million in NIL at Miami during the 2026 season alone. The Canes have produced two NFL Draft picks in the last two seasons. Cam Ward went No. 1 overall to the Tennessee Titans last year after transferring to Miami from Washington State in 2024. Carson Beck transferred from Georgia and led the Canes to their first national title game since 2002. Beck was drafted in the third round by the Arizona Cardinals earlier this year.   
 “I think the biggest thing was seeing what the last two quarterbacks at Miami really did,” he said in an interview with Locked On Canes on YouTube . “Going into the NFL and being a top five pick. Cam [Ward] did two years ago [Miami Hurricanes]. I think those were two of the two of the biggest reasons as to why I transferred.
 “But also just the opportunity to compete for a national championship was also a big one for me as well.”
 Mensah is projected as a first-round draft pick for 2027 per NFL Mock Draft Database. 
 MORE:   CFP rankings Week 11 winners (Notre Dame) and losers (Indiana, ACC) 
 Darian Mensah recruitment to Tulane
 Mensah's recruitment coming out of high school was a quiet one. He played high school football at St. Joseph, a small Catholic school in Santa Maria, Calif., on the central coast of the state. He was rated by the 247Sports Composite as a two-star prospect, checking in as the No. 161 quarterback in the class of 2023. He was rated as the No. 383 player out of his home state.
 He had just two offers coming out of high school. Tulane was the first, coming in August of his senior year. He was also offered by Idaho State and Lindenwood of the FCS. Mensah's tape came across then-Tulane head coach Willie Fritz's desk by way of his son, Wes.
 Per Yahoo Sports, Mensah's tape made its way to Wes. At the time, the Green Wave needed a quarterback.
 "We were scouring the country," Wes said via Yahoo Sports .
 "[It] apparently came across Coach Fritz's eye and desk and pushed towards his dad," Mensah's high school coach, Jose "Pepe" Villasenor said of his film via The Sporting News. "Like, hey, 'this kid has some Cali swag, and he has all the intangibles. 
 And from my understanding, that's when Coach Fritz had kind of pushed his son and whoever the area recruiter was to 'well, why don't you go check it out?' And they came out, came on campus, saw some film, met Mensah, met myself, talked to the athletic director to kind of really get a background on Darian. And thank God, a couple weeks later they gave him an official offer."
 Mensah signed with Tulane on National Signing Day in Feb. 2023 and enrolled in the summer. 
 ”It was one of those things where I was going through all kinds of people from all over," Wes added via The News & Observer . "And he stuck out to me on film.”
 Darian Mensah transfer timeline
 2023: Darian Mensah starts career at Tulane
 Mensah was recruited by former Green Wave head coach Willie Fritz and took a redshirt during his 2023 season. When Fritz left to take the head coaching job at Houston, Mensah remained at Tulane as the school hired Jon Sumrall. He competed with former four-star quarterback recruit Ty Thompson, who now plays tight end at Tulane, for the starting job ahead of the 2024 season.
 He won the starting job over Thompson, and Sumrall's decision paid off. Mensah led Tulane to an AAC title game berth and a 9-4 finish.
 Dec. 2024: Mensah enters the portal, commits to Duke
 Just a few days after Mensah entered the portal, he committed to Duke. The Blue Devils had gone 9-4 under first-year head coach Manny Diaz. Duke was in need of a quarterback, as starter Maliik Murphy entered the portal at the end of the season. 
 "I think just the opportunity to compete at an elite conference like the ACC, an elite head coach with Manny (Diaz)," Mensah said via the Fayetteville Observer of his decision in the summer of 2025. And an offense where you spread people out and throw the ball vertically."
 MORE:  College football picks, predictions against the spread for Week 11 matchups 
 Darian Mensah returns to Tulane with Duke
 Mensah has gone against his former team before. When he was at Duke last season, the Blue Devils played at Tulane for a Week 3 non-conference matchup. The quarterback was asked what it was going to be like going up against his former team ahead of the game. 
 "Yeah, it's definitely going to be a little bit weird going over there, my old team," Mensah told reporters . "But you know, once the ball's snapped, ball is ball and I'm sure Coach Sumrall's going to have them coached up and I think it's going to be a big time matchup."
 Mensah added that he saw Coach Sumrall over the summer at a wedding and that the coach "showed him some love" and understood his decision.  
 "What makes that place special is those coaches over there," Mensah also said. "They really care about their players and how they're doing so I think that's the hardest part is leaving those relationships behind. But Tulane was great to me. They gave me an opportunity to be where I'm at right now and I'm extremely grateful to those guys."  
 Naturally, Tulane fans weren't exactly too kind to Mensah upon his return. Fans were booing him even as he made it onto the field for warmups: 
 Although Mensah threw for 313 yards with three touchdowns and an interception, Tulane won the reunion game 34-27.  
 Darian Mensah prepares to play Duke with Miami
 Mensah will go through this process yet again this week, as the Hurricanes take on the Duke Blue Devils on Saturday. Luckily for Mensah, the game is at his home stadium in Miami Gardens.  
 "When I step onto the football field it's my team vs. your team and I'm trying to go execute," Mensah said of playing the Blue Devils . "And so, I never had any personal emotions but going into Tulane was definitely weird, just being on that opposite sideline to where I've always been was a little bit weird."
 Mensah's high school coach believes his former player will respond to the situation well: 
 "He's definitely emotionally prepared for that homecoming against Duke," Coach Villasenor said. "And he appreciates everything that he learned and what Duke did for him, so it isn't like he shuns Duke. You know, he loved his coaches there. He loved the community. He loved the school, and he loved the fact that they did believe in him and and you know offered him an opportunity there at Duke, and he won the ACC championship there. 
 And I would like to think that you know there's a lot of Duke fans that are appreciative of the efforts and the sacrifices and the successes that he had there to help Duke you know be a competitive team in the ACC."
